title: How to Pressure-Wash a Driveway

seo.title: How to Pressure-Wash a Driveway
seo.meta_description: Pressure-wash a driveway using the lowest effective pressure, a suitable fan nozzle, and steady distance. Protect joints, people, coatings, and drains.
seo.search_intent: Clean a concrete driveway with a pressure washer without etching the surface, forcing water into joints, or causing injection injuries.

excerpt: A pressure washer cleans quickly but can also etch concrete and cause serious injury. Technique matters more than using the highest pressure available.
content_html:
A pressure-washer jet can penetrate skin and damage concrete, wood, paint, and joints. Never aim it at people, pets, wiring, or your own feet to clean footwear.

Prepare the area before starting

Remove objects, sweep loose gravel, and protect or avoid delicate surfaces. Plan where runoff will go and keep dirt or chemicals out of storm drains.

Start with lower pressure and more distance

Use an appropriate fan nozzle rather than a concentrated jet and test an inconspicuous area. Move closer gradually only when needed.

Keep the spray moving evenly

Work in overlapping passes and do not hold the jet on one spot, which can carve lines or etch the slab.

Respect cracks, joints, and weak edges

Do not force high-pressure water at close range into expansion joints, cracks, or crumbling edges. Damaged concrete may need repair before aggressive cleaning.

Use detergent only when compatible

Follow the pressure-washer and product labels, and control runoff. Never mix chemicals in the machine unless the manufacturer specifically permits it.

For painted, sealed, or decorative concrete, always test first because pressure that is harmless on bare concrete may strip a coating.

faq.question: Which nozzle should I use?
faq.answer: Use a fan nozzle appropriate for the machine and surface, and do not begin with the most concentrated jet.

faq.question: Can I pressure-wash in sandals?
faq.answer: No. Wear closed footwear and keep the jet away from your body.

faq.question: Why am I getting stripes?
faq.answer: Uneven distance, speed, or overlap can leave visible cleaning lines; use consistent passes.
